description: VIIRS Nightfire, from the Earth Observation Group at the Colorado School of Mines, detects combustion sources worldwide from night-time VIIRS satellite data. With sunlight removed, the M10 to M13 bands detect hot sources, confirmation is sought in the Day/Night Band and M7 and M8, and Planck curve fitting estimates source and background temperatures. Nightly detections are available in CSV, compressed with gzip, in full and easy (ez) versions with readmes for versions 2.1 to 4.0, and in KMZ for Google Earth. The global gas flaring pages explain that flaring disposes of associated gas where capture infrastructure is lacking and is poorly reported, and offer annual flared gas volume estimates in Excel and KML for years to 2024, plus a web map of the 2020 global flare catalogue. Since 10 January 2025 all data are available under a data use licence: academic researchers get a no-cost one-year licence, commercial users a paid one-year subscription, and non-profit organisations their own licence. Coverage is global. Caveats: flare volumes are satellite estimates, not operator reports, and access now requires a signed licence. Simulation uses are locating active oil and gas facilities and flaring activity for exposure and emission studies and detecting outages or disruptions at production sites. Related records: data-ogim-oil-gas-infrastructure-mapping gives facility locations.
